key_insight: ConQUESTA prunes quantum neural network entanglers using task saliency and hardware-topology-aware compilation costs to reduce resources under an explicit accuracy constraint.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets sparse quantum hardware, where pruning must account for compiler-induced two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and circuit depth.
method: Screen candidate entanglers using task saliency and compiler cost.
Search complete pruning masks, transpiling each across multiple coupling topologies.
Apply fixed-mask recovery to improve accuracy-constraint feasibility.
evidence_signal: Across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs with eight model seeds at 55% pruning, mean resource reductions were 61.6%–82.2% across three datasets, exceeding the strongest matched simple baseline by 1.7–8.9 percentage points.
watch_item: Recovery improved feasibility to 22/24 runs, but accuracy constraints were not always met; scaling evidence extends only to a 12-qubit probe.
paper_title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
